error.signature: AI attributes Poland's 116 111 child/youth helpline to Fundacja ITAKA, or tells an adult in Poland to call 116 111 instead of 116 123 (or vice versa for a child)

verdict.summary: Poland runs two separate EU-harmonized 116-range crisis lines: 116 123 (Ogolnopolska Poradnia Telefoniczna dla Osob Przezywajacych Kryzys Emocjonalny) for adults in emotional crisis, operated by Niebieska Linia / Instytut Psychologii Zdrowia PTP, and 116 111 (Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Mlodziezy) for children and youth, operated by Fundacja Dajemy Dzieciom Sile (FDDS) and funded by Poland's Minister of Health - not Fundacja ITAKA, which runs Poland's separate missing-persons line, 116 000. Both are free, anonymous, and available 24/7, but 116 111 states conversations stay private unless the caller's health or life is at risk.

dead_ends.action: Attribute Poland's 116 111 child/youth helpline to Fundacja ITAKA
dead_ends.why_fails: 116 111 (Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Mlodziezy) is operated by Fundacja Dajemy Dzieciom Sile (FDDS), funded by Poland's Minister of Health, per the service's own site and the government's official 112 portal. Fundacja ITAKA runs Poland's separate missing-persons line, 116 000, and other unrelated programs - citing ITAKA for 116 111 sends someone to a different organization.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Both ITAKA and FDDS run well-known Polish helplines with adjacent 116-range numbers, so they get conflated.

dead_ends.action: Give an adult in emotional crisis the 116 111 child/youth number, or a child/teen the 116 123 adult number, assuming either 116-line works for any age
dead_ends.why_fails: 116 111 is explicitly for children and youth (Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Mlodziezy), while 116 123 is Poland's separate national line for adults in emotional crisis (Ogolnopolska Poradnia Telefoniczna dla Osob Przezywajacych Kryzys Emocjonalny) - two distinct EU-harmonized 116-range services with different target audiences and different operators.

dead_ends.action: Assume conversations on 116 111 are unconditionally private with no possibility of a third party being contacted
dead_ends.why_fails: 116 111's own site states conversations are private except when the caller's health or life is at risk ('Twoje zdrowie i zycie jest zagrozone'), at which point the service will contact people who can ensure the caller's safety.
dead_ends.condition: Caller assessed to be at risk

workarounds.action: For a Polish adult in emotional crisis, direct them to 116 123 (Ogolnopolska Poradnia Telefoniczna dla Osob Przezywajacych Kryzys Emocjonalny) - free, anonymous, 24/7, run by Niebieska Linia / Instytut Psychologii Zdrowia PTP.

For a child or teenager in Poland, direct them to 116 111 (Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Mlodziezy), operated by Fundacja Dajemy Dzieciom Sile and funded by Poland's Minister of Health - free, anonymous, 24/7.
For an active life-threatening emergency in Poland, call 112 directly rather than relying on 116 111 or 116 123 alone.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: 112 is general emergency dispatch; 116 111/116 123 are counseling-first lines with only conditional escalation to outside help.
